written_by: hand, from the RTL and the property text; never from sby output
step_rule: A concurrent property clocked on posedge clk samples the values of step k on the edge into step k+1, so sby reports it at step k+1. $past(x, n) on that edge reads step k-n; for k-n < 0 it reads state from before the trace began, which no constraint covers. Step 0 is the initial state; m_rst holds rst high at step 0.
timeline: W=8, D=4, count is 3 bits. Step 0 reset. Step 1: count=0, empty. One write per step from step 1 gives count=4 (full) at step 5.

ok.why: A write is accepted only when not full, so count never exceeds D. full and empty compare count against different constants. An accepted write without a read raises count by one. full can only rise on a step after a write. a_dis_ok is vacuous by construction (it is disabled exactly when its body is false), which is the check that disable iff is honoured.

bug.why: BUG_FULL accepts a write while full. Writes on steps 1 to 5 give count=5 at step 6, a_never_over samples it on the edge out of step 6, so the earliest failure is step 7. No shorter trace exists: count rises by at most one per step from 0 at step 1. abc pdr is not a bounded search and need not return the shortest counterexample, and sby replays only the last step of its witness, so the reported step may be later than 7; the trace must still show count above 4. Every other assertion still holds up to the first violation (a_cnt_up could only break on the 3-bit wrap at count=7).

dis.why: CHECK_DISABLE adds a_dis_bad, the same body as a_dis_ok without disable iff. rst is high at step 0, so a_dis_bad fails on the first edge, at step 1. a_dis_ok must not fail: if it did, disable iff would have been dropped.

cov.why: c_full: full is first possible at step 5, so it is reached at step 6. c_drain ($past(full, 4) && empty) is the pre-trace footgun. A witness that does not depend on pre-trace state needs full at step k-4 and empty at step k; full first holds at step 5 and four reads empty the FIFO by step 9, so a genuine witness cannot be reached before step 10. But on the edge out of step 1, $past(full, 4) reads step -3, which is unconstrained, and the FIFO is empty after reset, so the solver reaches c_drain at step 2 on a trace in which full is never 1. Reached here does not mean the FIFO ever drained from full.
